# Parameter perturbation and Poisson regularity {#sec-parameter-perturbation}

The contraction theorem is stated for each frozen parameter, with constants uniform on a specified region. We now compare two such frozen kernels, $Q_\theta$ and $Q_\vartheta$. The comparison is an operator calculation on Lipschitz test functions; it does not require constructing an additional coupling of the augmented transitions.

## One-step kernel regularity

For $f:\mathsf Z\to\mathbb{R}$ and $z=(x,u)$, write

$$
f_{\theta,u}(y)=f(y,T_\theta(y,u)).
$$ {#eq-pulled-back-test}

By @eq-augmented-kernel,

$$
Q_\theta f(x,u)=P_\theta f_{\theta,u}(x).
$$

Adding and subtracting $P_\vartheta f_{\theta,u}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)f(x,u)
={}&(P_\theta-P_\vartheta)f_{\theta,u}(x)\\
&+P_\vartheta(f_{\theta,u}-f_{\vartheta,u})(x).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-augmented-operator-perturbation}

Under @asm-memory-lipschitz, $\|f_{\theta,u}\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_X)}\leq(1+L_T)\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}$, and

$$
|f_{\theta,u}(y)-f_{\vartheta,u}(y)|
\leq\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}
d_Y(T_\theta(y,u),T_\vartheta(y,u)).
$$

Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality therefore yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
&W_{d_Z}(Q_\theta((x,u),\cdot),Q_\vartheta((x,u),\cdot))\\
&\quad\leq (1+L_T)W_{d_X}(P_\theta(x,\cdot),P_\vartheta(x,\cdot))\\
&\qquad+P_\vartheta\!\left[
d_Y(T_\theta(\cdot,u),T_\vartheta(\cdot,u))
\right](x).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-one-step-parameter-bound}

The first term measures the change in the driving kernel; the second measures the change in the memory update under the same driving law. For the affine EMA, the second term depends only on $b_\theta-b_\vartheta$, since $A$ is fixed. In the square-root coordinates of @eq-sqrt-memory-update it can be controlled instead by the parameter difference of the original innovation $H_\theta$.

::: {#asm-parameter-kernel}
## Driver-level parameter regularity

On a parameter region $\mathsf K$, assume there is a measurable $w:\mathsf X\to[1,\infty)$ and constants $L_P,L_{T,\theta}<\infty$, uniform over $\theta,\vartheta\in\mathsf K$, such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{d_X}(P_\theta(x,\cdot),P_\vartheta(x,\cdot))
&\leq L_P\|\theta-\vartheta\|w(x),\\
P_\vartheta[d_Y(T_\theta(\cdot,u),T_\vartheta(\cdot,u))](x)
&\leq L_{T,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|w(x)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-driver-parameter-assumptions}

for all $x$ and $u$ in the memory space under consideration. Let $\mathcal V:\mathsf Z\to[1,\infty)$ dominate $w(x)$ and suppose the family $(Q_\theta)_{\theta\in\mathsf K}$ has uniform geometric Wasserstein contraction as in @thm-wasserstein-lifting.
:::

The bounds in @asm-parameter-kernel are verification assumptions on the driver and forcing, not consequences of frozen contraction.

::: {#prp-augmented-kernel-regularity}
## One-step regularity of augmented kernels

Under @asm-memory-lipschitz and @asm-parameter-kernel,

$$
\gamma_{\theta,\vartheta}
:=\sup_{z\in\mathsf Z}
\frac{W_{d_Z}(Q_\theta(z,\cdot),Q_\vartheta(z,\cdot))}
{\mathcal V(z)}
\leq L_Q\|\theta-\vartheta\|,
$$ {#eq-augmented-perturbation-gamma}

with $L_Q=(1+L_T)L_P+L_{T,\theta}$. Equivalently, for every $d_Z$-Lipschitz test $f$,

$$
|(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)f(z)|
\leq L_Q\|\theta-\vartheta\|\mathcal V(z)
\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}.
$$ {#eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound}
:::

::: {.proof}
Apply @eq-one-step-parameter-bound, substitute @eq-driver-parameter-assumptions and divide by $\mathcal V(z)\geq w(x)$. The equivalent operator estimate is the dual representation of $W_{d_Z}$.
:::

## Perturbation of invariant laws

The geometric estimate of @thm-wasserstein-lifting and the weighted one-step bound enter the Wasserstein perturbation framework of [@RudolfSchweizer2018, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.1]. The stationary estimate below uses the invariant weighted moment directly; a Lyapunov inequality is one way to obtain that moment. Its proof retains the operator calculation needed for Poisson regularity.

::: {#cor-invariant-parameter}
## Lipschitz dependence of augmented invariant laws

Suppose $Q_\theta$ has invariant law $\nu_\theta\in\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$, satisfies @eq-augmented-contraction and obeys @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound, as supplied by @prp-augmented-kernel-regularity. Suppose also that

$$
\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)\leq M_{\mathcal V}<\infty.
$$ {#eq-uniform-invariant-moment}

Then for every $\theta,\vartheta\in\mathsf K$,

$$
W_{d_Z}(\nu_\theta,\nu_\vartheta)
\leq \frac{C_Z(\eta)L_QM_{\mathcal V}}{1-\eta}
\|\theta-\vartheta\|.
$$ {#eq-invariant-parameter-regularity}
:::

::: {.proof}
Fix a $1$-Lipschitz $f$. Since $\nu_\theta$ and $\nu_\vartheta$ are invariant,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\nu_\theta(f)-\nu_\vartheta(f)|
\leq{}&
|(\nu_\theta-\nu_\vartheta)(Q_\theta^n f)|\\
&+|\nu_\vartheta(Q_\theta^nf-Q_\vartheta^nf)|.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first term is at most $C_Z(\eta)\eta^n W_{d_Z}(\nu_\theta,\nu_\vartheta)$. For the second use

$$
Q_\theta^n-Q_\vartheta^n
=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}Q_\vartheta^j
(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)Q_\theta^{n-1-j}.
$$ {#eq-perturbation-telescope}

The stationarity of $\nu_\vartheta$, @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound and the bound
$\|Q_\theta^k f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^k$
give

$$
|\nu_\vartheta(Q_\theta^nf-Q_\vartheta^nf)|
\leq C_Z(\eta)L_Q\|\theta-\vartheta\|\,
\nu_\vartheta(\mathcal V)\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\eta^{n-1-j}.
$$

Let $n\to\infty$. The first term tends to zero, and the geometric sum is bounded by $(1-\eta)^{-1}$. Taking the supremum over $f$ proves @eq-invariant-parameter-regularity.
:::

Uniform drift constants in @eq-augmented-drift, together with suitable moment conditions, provide one route to @eq-uniform-invariant-moment. The constants in @eq-invariant-parameter-regularity depend on the contraction, moment and perturbation bounds on $\mathsf K$.

## Regularity of the stationary mean field

Suppose $G_\theta:\mathsf Z\to\mathbb{R}^d$ has a uniform Lipschitz seminorm and satisfies

$$
\|G_\theta(z)-G_\vartheta(z)\|
\leq L_{G,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|\mathcal V(z).
$$ {#eq-observable-parameter-assumption}

For $F(\theta)=\nu_\theta(G_\theta)$, add and subtract $\nu_\vartheta(G_\theta)$ to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|F(\theta)-F(\vartheta)\|
\leq{}&
\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\,
W_{d_Z}(\nu_\theta,\nu_\vartheta)\\
&+\nu_\vartheta(\|G_\theta-G_\vartheta\|).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-field-parameter-bound}

Thus @cor-invariant-parameter gives local Lipschitz regularity of $F$ under @eq-observable-parameter-assumption. For the square-root memory coordinates of @eq-adam-lipschitz-readout the readout is independent of $\theta$, so the second term vanishes. This Lipschitz bound will also supply the regularity of the limiting ODE field.

## Eccentricity and weighted growth

Write $E_{1,\theta}(z)=\int d_Z(z,z')\,\nu_\theta(dz')$ for the first eccentricity. Suppose $E_{1,\theta}(z)\leq C_E\mathcal V(z)$ uniformly for $\theta\in\mathsf K$. Centring a Lipschitz function under $\nu_\theta$ gives

$$
\|f-\nu_\theta(f)\|_{\mathcal V}
\leq C_E\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}.
$$ {#eq-eccentricity-weighted-embedding}

Indeed, $|f(z)-\nu_\theta(f)|\leq\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}E_{1,\theta}(z)$. The triangle inequality also gives

$$
E_{1,\theta}(z)
\leq d_Z(z,z_0)+\nu_\theta(d_Z(z_0,\cdot)).
$$

Consequently the comparison is uniform if $d_Z(z,z_0)\leq c\mathcal V(z)$ and $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)<\infty$. For a zero-mass signed measure $\xi$ with finite weighted variation, define $\|\xi\|_{\mathrm{KR}}=\sup_{\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\leq1}|\xi(f)|$. Subtracting $\nu_\theta(f)$ inside $\xi(f)$ and using the same embedding gives

$$
\|\xi\|_{\mathrm{KR}}
\leq C_E\int\mathcal V(z)\,|\xi|(dz).
$$ {#eq-weighted-to-wasserstein}

Eccentricity thus links the Lipschitz estimates obtained from Wasserstein contraction to the weighted-growth estimates used in [@Care2026].

## Frozen Poisson solution

For a scalar Lipschitz observable $G_\theta$, set $\bar G_\theta=G_\theta-F(\theta)$ as in @eq-augmented-poisson; vector-valued observables are treated coordinatewise. Geometric Wasserstein contraction and finite first eccentricity give the unique centred Lipschitz solution [@Hofstadler2026, Theorem 3.4], represented by @eq-poisson-series, with $\nu_\theta(u_\theta)=0$ and

$$
\|u_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}
\leq\Lambda_\theta\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)},
\qquad
\Lambda_\theta:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n)
\leq\frac{C_Z(\eta)}{1-\eta}.
$$ {#eq-poisson-lipschitz-bound}

To see the summability directly, Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality gives

$$
|Q_\theta^nG_\theta(z)-F(\theta)|
\leq \tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n)
\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}E_{1,\theta}(z).
$$ {#eq-frozen-centred-decay}

The right-hand side is summable in $n$. It is also integrable under $\nu_\theta$, since $\nu_\theta\in\mathcal P_1$. Thus termwise integration centres the solution, and shifting the series proves @eq-augmented-poisson. If two centred Lipschitz solutions existed, their difference $v$ would satisfy $v=Q_\theta^n v$ for every $n$; contraction forces its Lipschitz seminorm to vanish, and centring then gives $v=0$.

Applying the Neumann-series bound yields

$$
\|u_\theta\|_{\mathcal V}
\leq C_E\Lambda_\theta\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}.
$$ {#eq-poisson-weighted-growth}

The pointwise estimate $|u_\theta(z)|\leq\Lambda_\theta\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}E_{1,\theta}(z)$ also gives stationary $L^p$ bounds whenever $\nu_\theta(E_{1,\theta}^p)<\infty$ [@Hofstadler2026, Theorem 3.5]. For bounded innovations, @eq-adam-readout-lipschitz verifies the Lipschitz readout hypothesis for Adam.

## Parameter regularity of the Poisson solution

The weighted one-step perturbation bound of @prp-augmented-kernel-regularity combines with the decay of centred iterates to give a parameter modulus for the Poisson solution. This follows the comparison-of-iterates approach of [@Care2026, Theorem 2], using Wasserstein contraction on the augmented space.

::: {#prp-poisson-parameter}
## Log-Lipschitz parameter regularity

Let $\mathsf K$ be a compact parameter set. Assume uniformly over $\theta,\vartheta\in\mathsf K$ that:

1. $Q_\theta$ satisfies @eq-augmented-contraction with common constants $C_Z<\infty$ and $\rho\in(0,1)$, and has invariant law $\nu_\theta\in\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$.
2. The one-step weighted estimate @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound holds, and $Q_\theta\mathcal V\leq a\mathcal V+b$ for some $0\leq a<1$, $b<\infty$.
3. $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)<\infty$ and $d_Z(z,z_0)\leq c\mathcal V(z)$ for some $z_0$.
4. $\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\leq L_G$ and
   $|G_\theta(z)-G_\vartheta(z)|\leq L_{G,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|\mathcal V(z)$.

Assume the kernels and observables are jointly measurable in parameter and state. For $t>0$, set $\omega(t)=t(1+\log^+(1/t))$ and $\omega(0)=0$. Then there is $C<\infty$ such that

$$
|u_\theta(z)-u_\vartheta(z)|
\leq C\mathcal V(z)\omega(\|\theta-\vartheta\|).
$$ {#eq-poisson-parameter-log-lipschitz}

The same estimate holds for $\phi_\theta=Q_\theta u_\theta$:

$$
|\phi_\theta(z)-\phi_\vartheta(z)|
\leq C\mathcal V(z)\omega(\|\theta-\vartheta\|).
$$ {#eq-poisson-feedback-log-lipschitz}
:::

::: {.proof}
Put $\delta=\|\theta-\vartheta\|$ and write

$$
R_\theta^nG_\theta(z)=Q_\theta^nG_\theta(z)-F(\theta),
\qquad
D_n(z)=R_\theta^nG_\theta(z)-R_\vartheta^nG_\vartheta(z).
$$

The drift assumption gives $\sup_{\theta,n}Q_\theta^n\mathcal V(z)\leq C_V\mathcal V(z)$. By the eccentricity comparison and @eq-invariant-wasserstein-rate,

$$
|R_\theta^nG_\theta(z)|
\leq C_Z\rho^n L_GE_{1,\theta}(z)
\leq C_1\rho^n\mathcal V(z),
$$

so $|D_n(z)|\leq 2C_1\rho^n\mathcal V(z)$.

For a second bound, decompose

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_n={}&(Q_\theta^n-Q_\vartheta^n)G_\theta\\
&+Q_\vartheta^n(G_\theta-G_\vartheta)
-\bigl(F(\theta)-F(\vartheta)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$

The last term is $O(\delta)$ by @eq-field-parameter-bound and @cor-invariant-parameter. The middle term is at most $L_{G,\theta}C_V\delta\mathcal V(z)$. For the first term, telescope as in @eq-perturbation-telescope. Wasserstein contraction gives

$$
\|Q_\theta^kG_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}
\leq C_Z\rho^kL_G.
$$

Applying @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound inside the telescoping sum,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&|(Q_\theta^n-Q_\vartheta^n)G_\theta(z)|\\
&\quad\leq C_ZL_QL_G\delta
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\rho^{n-1-j}Q_\vartheta^j\mathcal V(z)\\
&\quad\leq \frac{C_ZL_QL_GC_V}{1-\rho}\,
\delta\mathcal V(z).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-centred-iterate-parameter-bound}

Thus $|D_n(z)|\leq C_2\delta\mathcal V(z)$, uniformly in $n$. Combining the two estimates and summing the Neumann series yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
|u_\theta(z)-u_\vartheta(z)|
&\leq C_3\mathcal V(z)
\sum_{n=0}^\infty\min\{\delta,\rho^n\}\\
&\leq C_4\mathcal V(z)\omega(\delta).
\end{aligned}
$$

For $0<\delta<1$, choose $N=\lceil\log(1/\delta)/|\log\rho|\rceil$. The first $N$ terms contribute at most $N\delta$ and the remaining terms at most $\rho^N/(1-\rho)\leq\delta/(1-\rho)$. For $\delta\geq1$ the geometric bound suffices, and $\delta=0$ is immediate. Finally, the Poisson identity gives $\phi_\theta=u_\theta-G_\theta+F(\theta)$. The parameter estimates for its three terms prove @eq-poisson-feedback-log-lipschitz.
:::

The parameter modulus follows from the weighted one-step perturbation bound @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound. Its logarithmic term measures the number of iterations required for geometric forgetting to reach the scale of a parameter change.
